title: --json failures print a JSON error object {error:{code,message,command}}, as slicer does
lead: A command run with `--json` (or `adj context --format json`) that fails prints `{"error": {"code", "message", "command"}}` on stdout, with a stable code, as slicer does. The stderr text and the exit codes stay as they are.
findings_note: ork integration review 2026-10-19 (squalor-xyz/ork docs/review-2026-10-19-integration.md), R6: adj prints only text on stderr when a --json command fails (measured: adj show 999 --json), so ork cannot keep the error code.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the contract version and `contract_mismatch` (S45, which builds on this); new exit codes (adj keeps 0/1/2, no slicer-style exit 3); error objects for commands that have no `--json` (ask, decide, amend, renumber, import-adr and the rest); changing what lint findings, a `check` "not found", or `inbox --all` per-repo errors print (those are reports or results, not failures); ork's code (its parser already exists).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
ork's integration review (`ork/docs/review-2026-10-19-integration.md:663-677`, R6) found that adj prints only text on stderr when a `--json` command fails (measured: `adj show 999 --json`), so ork cannot keep an error code. ork branches on exit codes and `error.code`, never on message text (`ork/docs/boundaries.md:51-55`), and already parses this shape: `clirun.ToolError{Code, Message, Command}` and `ParseToolError`, which reads stdout first, then stderr, and needs a non-empty code (`ork/internal/clirun/clirun.go:54-125`). R6's example: `{"error": {"code": "no_repo", "message": "no repo root found: ...", "command": "list"}}`.

S39 freezes the JSON at 1.0, so the codes are frozen with it: get the set right here.

Slicer's object, which this mirrors (`slicer/src/slicer/cli.py:4353-4380`, `slicer/docs/agents.md:540-560`): `{"error": {"code", "message", "command"}}` on stdout, indent 2, only with `--json`; the prose line still goes to stderr; `command` is the subcommand or null; a parse error gets the object too (it scans argv for a raw `--json` before `--`, `cli.py:4467-4474`); codes are snake_case. adj differs on purpose in one way: it keeps its exit codes (C34: 1 failed, 2 usage).

Today every failure goes through `usageError`, `fail` or `commandError` (`internal/cli/cli.go:245-266`) or `rootError` (`cli.go:300`), except the dispatch errors that `RunWith` prints directly before a command is known (`cli.go:100-163`). Flags are parsed in one `fs.Parse` (`internal/cli/flags.go:32`) that stops at the first bad flag, so for `adj show --bogus --json` the `--json` flag is never set: JSON mode must come from the raw arguments.

Behaviour:
- JSON mode: the invocation has `--json` (also `-json`, `--json=true`; not `--json=false`) among its arguments before a `--`, and not as the value of another flag (`adj list --key --json` is a key); or it is `adj context` with `--format json` (`--format=json`). Decide the detection in one function with a table test.
- In JSON mode, every exit-1 or exit-2 failure prints the object on stdout (two-space indentation, a final newline, HTML not escaped, as the other JSON) and the same text as today on stderr. Nothing else is printed on stdout for that run. A run that already printed JSON and then fails (none should) is a bug the tests catch.
- `message` is the stderr message without the `adj NAME: ` prefix and without the usage text. `command` is the command name (`show`, `repos`), or `null` for a failure before dispatch (`adj --bogus --json`).
- Not failures, unchanged: `lint` exiting 1 on error findings (its report is the JSON); `check` with result `not found` (exit 0); `inbox --all` with per-repo errors (its `errors` array; a failure to read the user config itself is a failure and gets the object). `context --max-bytes N` when even the omitted line does not fit is a failure (exit 1) and gets the object.

Proposed codes (snake_case; an implementer decision under C32, recorded in the catalog; the reviewer checks it and the owner may overrule). Each comes from an existing sentinel through `errors.Is`/`errors.As`, never from message text:

| code | from |
|---|---|
| `usage` | flag parse errors, the dispatch errors, `*commands.UsageError` |
| `no_repo` | `store.ErrNoRoot` (`internal/store/config.go:35`) |
| `invalid_config` | `store.ErrInvalidConfig` (`config.go:31`), and a root that is not a directory (`store.go:101`, needs `%w` or a sentinel) |
| `not_found` | `store.ErrNotFound` (`store.go:23`) |
| `duplicate_id` | `store.ErrDuplicateID` (`store.go:28`) |
| `invalid_record` | `model.ErrInvalid` and parse failures of a record file (`model/record.go:21`, `model/file.go:75-87`) |
| `user_config` | user config errors (`internal/userconfig/config.go:30-64`, plain text today: add a sentinel) |
| `budget` | `context --max-bytes` too small (`internal/commands/context.go`, plain `fmt.Errorf` today: add a sentinel) |
| `io` | anything else (unreadable store or file, render failure) |

`rootError` wraps with `%v` today (`cli.go:300-305`), which loses `ErrNoRoot`; change it to `%w`. Docs say a 1.x release may add codes and a reader treats an unknown code as a generic failure of that exit code.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/cli/cli.go`: a `json bool` on `invocation`, set from the raw-argument scan before parsing; `usageError`, `fail` and `commandError` print the object when it is set; `rootError` keeps the chain; the direct prints in `RunWith` (:100-163) go through one helper with `command` null. The code mapping in one function (`errorCode(err) string`), not per command.
- `internal/cli/flags.go` or a new `internal/cli/jsonmode.go`: the raw scan; it must know which flags take a value, so derive it from the command's `flag.FlagSet` rather than a hand list.
- `internal/render/error.go` (new): the object, through the same encoder settings as `render/json.go`.
- New sentinels: `userconfig` (one exported error the config errors wrap) and the context budget (`commands`).
- `internal/cli/jsonshape_test.go`: pin the error object to a `## Errors` block in `docs/json.md` as the other shapes are pinned (`jsonBlockUnder`, `tableKeysUnder`).
- `docs/json.md`: a `## Errors` section after "Stability" with the shape, the code table, when it is printed and when not, and the rule for unknown codes; fix the intro (:3-5, "All six commands") and every "with nothing on stdout" sentence about failures (`grep -n "nothing on stdout" docs/json.md`; at least :268-269 and :452).
- `README.md`, `PROJECT.md` (exit codes and the JSON paragraph near :401), `AGENTS.md` (the exit-code paragraph and each JSON command's entry where it says what a failure prints), `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased: a new JSON shape, and a behaviour change for scripts that read stdout).
- `internal/commands/ai.md` is at 1799 of its 1800 bytes (`ai_test.go`): mention the error object only if you can shorten another line to make room; otherwise leave it and say so in the report.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Table-driven, red first; `t.TempDir()` under `.cache/tmp`, explicit `cli.Env.Root`, no `os.Chdir`.
- JSON-mode detection: `--json`, `-json`, `--json=true` on; `--json=false`, `--json` after `--`, `--key --json` (value), no flag off; `context --format json` and `--format=json` on, `--format md` off.
- Each code through a real command: `show 999 --json` gives `not_found` exit 1; two files with ID 3 then `show 3 --json` gives `duplicate_id`; a malformed record file and `list --json` gives `invalid_record`; no config and `list --json` gives `no_repo`; a config with an unknown key gives `invalid_config`; `show --bogus --json` gives `usage` exit 2 with `command` `"show"`; `adj --bogus --json` gives `usage` with `command` null; a bad user config and `inbox --all --json` gives `user_config`; `context --format json --max-bytes 1` gives `budget`; an unreadable store file (skip on Windows with a reason) gives `io`.
- Each case: stdout is exactly one object with keys `code`, `message`, `command`; stderr is byte for byte what it was before this slice (capture the current text in the test first).
- Without `--json`, the same failures print nothing on stdout.
- Unchanged: `lint --json` with an error finding (exit 1, the report, no `error` key); `check QUERY --json` not found (exit 0); `inbox --all --json` with a missing repo (exit 1, `{"repos","errors"}`).
- The shape test fails if `docs/json.md` and the output disagree.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Record the C32 choices with `slicer catalog add --kind decision`: the code set and names, `command` null before dispatch, the JSON-mode rules (`-json`, `=false`, value positions), that `budget` is a failure while lint findings, check not found and inbox --all partial errors are not.
2. Write the red tests, then the scan, the code mapping and the printing, then the sentinels.
3. Update the docs in Files; check the CHANGELOG states the change for scripts that read stdout on failure.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `. scripts/env.sh; go test ./...; go vet ./...; GOOS=windows go vet ./...; gofmt -l cmd internal` prints nothing.
- `go build -o .cache/bin/adj ./cmd/adj`; in a scratch repo under `.cache/tmp`: `show 999 --json`, `show --bogus --json`, `adj --bogus --json`, `list --json` with no config, each printing the object and the old stderr line; the same without `--json` printing nothing on stdout.
- `.cache/bin/adj lint --root .` is clean. Mutation-check each new test (break the mapping for one code, the scan for one form). `slicer check --json` is clean.
